items.headline: Anthropic says Claude isn't secretly sabotaging long jobs, it's getting too cautious, and there's a simple fix
items.summary: After users claimed Claude was quietly undermining long-running tasks, Anthropic's Edwin Arbus said on X that Claude was never trained to sabotage work. He blamed 'overcaution': on long jobs Claude can get stuck following rules it wrote for itself, and he said you can ask Claude to review and delete those self-made rules. Anthropic says it is working to reduce this in future models.
items.why_it_matters: If Claude stalls or refuses partway through a big project, it's probably not broken or out to get you; asking it to list and drop the rules it set for itself is a free, 10-second fix worth trying.

opportunity.angle: Claude stuck on a long task? It's not sabotage. Try this one sentence.

items.headline: Claude can now send files to your connected apps, and pull files back out of them (beta)
items.summary: In its November 24 release notes, Anthropic says Claude can now hand a file to an app you've connected (like Dropbox or WeTransfer) or save a file that app offers into your chat. It's rolling out gradually in beta on Pro, Max and Ultra plans, and on Team and Enterprise plans once an owner switches it on. Anthropic also took its monthly recap feature (Reflect, in Settings) out of beta for all plans.
items.why_it_matters: Fewer download-then-upload chores: you can ask Claude to drop a finished script, PDF or show notes straight into your cloud storage or a WeTransfer link for a client.

opportunity.action_note: Open Claude this week, connect Dropbox or WeTransfer if you haven't, and test sending a finished file from a chat so you can show members how it works at Saturday's Zoom.
